dedupe_keys.name: faa advisory circular 150 5320 6g airport pavement design and evaluation subgrade and soil investigation guidance

description: FAA Advisory Circular 150/5320-6G, dated 7 June 2021 (Change 1), is the US guidance for designing and evaluating pavements used by aircraft at civil airports; it cancels AC 150/5320-6F of 2016. Contents: soil investigations and subgrade evaluation (soil surveys, number, location and depth of borings, boring logs, classification with the Unified Soil Classification System, moisture-density tests, California Bearing Ratio and subgrade stabilisation), frost and permafrost design, flexible and rigid pavement design with the FAARFIELD 2.0 software, maintenance and rehabilitation, and pavement strength reporting under the ICAO ACR-PCR protocol, with appendices on nondestructive testing, dynamic cone penetrometer and ground penetrating radar. Coverage: US civil airports; its use is mandatory for projects funded by the Airport Improvement Program and Passenger Facility Charges. Format and access: a 195-page PDF on the FAA site. Licence and cost: free US government publication. Caveats: a design standard, not a dataset of soils; site values come from each airport's own geotechnical report. Its soil classes, frost rules and strength parameters can set subgrade properties and pavement capacity for hazard exposure and capacity planning models of runways and taxiways. It relates to the FAA runway simulator and the AirTOP simulator in the catalogue.
